answers.rationale: I'm a pragmatic developer who values safety checks. Inline diffs give me visibility and control—I'd definitely use this feature because I can catch issues before they hit my codebase. The review step is essential for me to trust autonomous edits.

Rollback capability is a game-changer for me. Knowing I can undo changes instantly removes the biggest friction point in delegating complex tasks to an agent. This single feature would make me significantly more willing to let Claude Code work autonomously.

My main worry is that the agent might introduce subtle logic errors or break existing functionality in ways that aren't immediately obvious. Even with diffs, catching all edge cases is hard. I'm less concerned about security or autonomy—those feel manageable with checkpoints.

answers.value: Adding or updating unit tests for existing functions
answers.rationale: Tests are a safe boundary—high stakes are lower, easy to validate, and I can quickly spot if something's wrong. I'd start there before trusting the agent with core business logic or refactoring critical paths.
